newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil up on fresh hedge.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil up on fresh hedge.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps rose at midday as players came out to hedge their 1.35 million barrel physical sales to two local traders late Tuesday, traders said on Wednesday.
"The market rebounded after the large purchases on Tuesday night," brokers said.
The front month April gas oil was last quoted at $26.30/$26.60 per barrel, up from Tuesday's $26.00/$26.30, brokers said.
May gas oil was also quoted firmer at $25.20/$25.40, from Tuesday's $24.90/$25.05, they said.
Brokers said the market firmed after some players came in to hedge their earlier physical sales to local traders, Hin Leong and Sanko.
But swap sellers have raised their offers in reaction to the big demand and deals were few, they said.
Traders said the market was caught completely off-guard by the latest Hin Leong purchase, which combined with sister-company Sanko's purchases, totalled 1.35 million in nine cargoes.
Since March 3, the two companies have bought more than 10 million barrels of gas oil for loading from end March to early May.
The April jet fuel/gas oil regrade widened futher after Tuesday's physical sell-off.
April regrade was last quoted at -$1.30/-$1.05 per barrel, from Tuesday's -$1.25/-$1.00, brokers said.

In the physical market, jet fuel traded at $24.75 per barrel, down about 30 cents from the last week's traded level. But on a cost-and-freight basis a 200,000-barrel cargo traded at $24.00 per barrel.
Fuel oil swaps steady after the recent rally with April swaps quoted at $98.50/$99.50 per tonne.
